memos.headline: S09 and S07 Lead on Momentum; S04 and S03 in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S09 and S07 are the standout leaders—both up ~31% over 12 weeks with relative strength vs SPY near +30%, trading within 4% of 52-week highs, and well above their 200-day means (+29.8% and +46.5% respectively). S01 is also strong with RSI at 72 and 4w relative strength of +12.7%, though the overbought reading warrants caution. On the other side, S04 is in a severe downtrend: -27.5% from its 52-week high, RSI 36.4, 12w relative strength vs SPY of -20.2%, and trading nearly 19% below its 200-day mean—this is a broken chart. S03 is similarly weak at -17.3% from highs with persistent negative relative strength. I would pair long momentum names against the laggards and watch for any stabilization in the oversold group before reconsidering.

Massive uptrend (+77.8% 26w) with strong relative strength, RSI 57.9 still has room; extended vs 200d (+46.5%) is a risk—would cut on a close below 665.
Strong 4w momentum (+11.5%) and relative strength (+12.7% vs SPY), but RSI 72 signals near-term overbought; would trim on a break below 158.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, expanding earnings power and those suffering margin erosion. S10 stands out with 73.2% YoY revenue growth, a 63.1% net margin, and near-doubled net income (+94.5% YoY) on just $8.47B of total debt—this is the cleanest fundamental profile in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at a 47.3% net margin with net income up 59.5% YoY, though its $40.26B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other side, S02's 2.1% net margin and 61.2% YoY net income decline signal serious earnings deterioration despite top-line growth of 12.2%, and S09's revenue contraction (-1.3%) paired with a 14.6% net income decline on a thin 7.9% margin makes it hard to own. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and S09 before reconsidering; for S10 and S04, any deceleration in revenue growth or margin compression would change my view.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, 73.2% revenue growth, 94.5% net income growth, and minimal leverage ($8.47B debt) make this the strongest fundamental story in the universe.
47.3% net margin and 59.5% YoY net income growth demonstrate exceptional earnings power, though $40.26B in debt requires monitoring.
Solid 30.3% net margin, 18% revenue growth, 29.8% net income growth, and low leverage at $14.79B debt support a durable earnings profile.
Revenue of $143.76B and 29.3% net margin are healthy, but 15.7% revenue growth is decelerating relative to peers and $88.50B in total debt is elevated.
Largest revenue base at $213.39B but only 9.9% net margin and net income growth of just 5.9% YoY lag the top-line expansion of 13.6%.

A 2.1% net margin and 61.2% YoY net income collapse despite 12.2% revenue growth points to severe cost or competitive pressure.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Benign Inflation—Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Banks Over Defensives
memos.body: I see a clear easing regime: the fed funds upper bound is at 3.75%, down 75bp over the past year and 25bp over the last three months, while CPI is running at just 2.4% YoY—comfortably near target. The unemployment rate at 4.30% has drifted up 30bp YoY but ticked down 10bp over three months, suggesting a soft-landing labor market rather than outright deterioration. The 10y yield at 3.97% is down 32bp YoY and the 2s10s curve has steepened 40bp to +0.60pp, a textbook normalization that benefits banks' net interest margins and supports duration-sensitive equities. I have conviction that this mid-cycle easing backdrop favors growth and financials; a CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment spiking above 4.5% would force me to revisit the regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits most from falling rates and a steepening curve in a benign inflation environment.
Banks gain from curve steepening (+40bp YoY in 2s10s) and continued easing supporting credit demand.
Cyclicals should hold up as the labor market stabilizes and easing supports economic activity without overheating.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; moderate growth and stable inflation leave the sector range-bound.
Staples lose relative appeal as easing favors risk assets, though they remain a hedge if unemployment surprises higher.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit from the 75bp cumulative cut and further easing expectations embedded in the curve.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Crushed, S07 and S01 Stand Out Positively
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. S02 dropped -19.6% on its Jan-27 results and just filed a management change on Feb-25, suggesting ongoing negative narrative pressure that likely has not fully resolved. S04 fell -10.0% on Jan-28 results with no subsequent positive catalysts filed. On the constructive side, S07 posted a +3.4% reaction on Jan-29 earnings and S01 gained +2.6% on Jan-22 results, both accompanied by Reg FD disclosures that signal proactive investor communication. S10's fresh -5.5% drop on Feb-25 earnings is very recent and sentiment is likely still deteriorating, while S08, S05, and S09 showed muted reactions near zero, leaving me with low conviction on those names.

views.note: A -19.6% earnings reaction is an extreme negative sentiment shock, and the subsequent executive departure on Feb-25 reinforces instability.
A -10.0% post-earnings drop with no offsetting positive filings since suggests sentiment remains deeply negative.
Fresh -5.5% earnings reaction just one day old means negative sentiment is still being digested and likely not yet fully priced.
A +3.4% earnings reaction and proactive Reg FD disclosure point to constructive sentiment momentum.
Positive +2.6% earnings reaction paired with multiple Reg FD filings suggests management is actively shaping a favorable narrative.
A -5.6% earnings reaction on Feb-05 with no subsequent positive catalysts keeps sentiment negative.
Despite a -4.2% earnings drop in Jan, high filing volume including management changes and multiple Reg FD disclosures clouds the picture.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and routine governance filings leave no strong sentiment signal either way.
Near-flat -0.5% earnings reaction and a subsequent Other Events filing provide no clear directional sentiment read.
Flat +0.6% earnings reaction and a recent officer change filing leave sentiment ambiguous.

memos.headline: Rising Policy Uncertainty and Oil Prices Signal Elevated Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a sharp acceleration in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, now at 319 — up nearly 38% over three months — alongside a VIX that has climbed 15% in the past month to 18.63, suggesting markets are pricing in meaningful policy-driven tail risk. WTI crude at $65.10 is up almost 11% over three months, which I read as reflecting tightening energy-security conditions, possibly linked to sanctions enforcement or supply disruptions. High-yield spreads have widened modestly (+29bp in a month to 2.98%) but remain historically tight, so credit markets are not yet in panic — this looks like a slow-burn structural shift rather than a one-quarter event. S06 stands out with four 8-K filings in six weeks (a mix of Reg FD and Other Events), which could indicate the company is navigating rapidly changing regulatory or geopolitical conditions. I would need to see explicit sanctions designations, new export-control rules, or a reversal in oil supply trends to change my current cautious posture.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K filing frequency in a rising policy-uncertainty environment suggests the company faces elevated regulatory or geopolitical exposure.
Two Reg FD filings in January are routine; no specific geopolitical signal, but the macro backdrop warrants caution.
Two Reg FD disclosures in January appear standard; I lack evidence of direct sanctions or export-control exposure but the elevated uncertainty index keeps me from going long.
Single 8.01 filing in mid-February is ambiguous; without detail on the event, I cannot distinguish geopolitical risk from routine disclosure.
One Reg FD filing in late January is unremarkable; holding neutral pending clarity on any policy-driven headwinds.
Single Reg FD disclosure in January with no geopolitical red flags, but rising oil prices and policy uncertainty warrant monitoring.
